learn: Every person is special. You have a name, a birthday and things you like to do.
Some people like to paint. Some like to run. Some like to read. What do you like?
Being yourself is a good thing.
check: Does every person have something special about them?
Which is something you might like to do?
lessons.try: Draw a picture of something you love to do.

learn: People are alike in some ways. We all need food, sleep and friends.
People are different in some ways. We may look different, speak different languages or like different foods.
Differences make the world interesting. We treat everyone with kindness.
check: We all need food and sleep
We all have the same name
We all like the same food
How do we treat people who are different from us?
lessons.try: Find one way you and a friend are alike and one way you are different.

learn: It is good to know your full name.
It is good to know a trusted grown-up's phone number, so you can get help if you are lost.
Keep this information private online. Only share it with trusted grown-ups, police or teachers.
check: Why should you know a grown-up's phone number?
So you can get help if you are lost
To call anyone on the internet
Who can you share your phone number with?
What should you know about yourself?
lessons.try: Practise saying your full name and a grown-up's phone number with a family member.

learn: A family is a group of people who love and care for each other.
Families come in many sizes. Some have one parent, some have two, some live with grandparents, aunts or foster parents.
Every kind of family is a real family.
check: People who love and care for each other
Do all families look the same?
Can a grandparent be part of a family you live with?
lessons.try: Draw the people in your family.

learn: Family members help each other.
They share chores like setting the table, feeding a pet or putting toys away.
When everyone helps, the work is done faster and there is more time to play.
check: So the work is done faster
lessons.try: Choose one chore to do for your family today.

learn: A tradition is something a family does again and again, often on special days.
A tradition could be a special meal, a song, a game or a story told every year.
Traditions help families remember and feel close.
check: Something a family does again and again
lessons.try: Ask a grown-up about a tradition in your family.

learn: Rules tell us how to act.
Rules keep us safe and help things be fair.
Without rules, games and classrooms would be confusing.
check: Keep us safe and make things fair
lessons.try: Name a rule from a game you play.

learn: At school we raise our hand to talk, so everyone gets a turn.
We walk in the hall, so nobody gets hurt.
We keep our hands to ourselves and use kind words.
check: Why do we raise our hand to talk?
How do we move in the hall?
lessons.try: Tell a grown-up why we walk in the hall.

learn: There are rules at home too, like washing hands before eating or putting toys away.
If someone breaks a rule, there can be a consequence. A consequence is what happens because of a choice.
A good consequence can come from a good choice, too, like a clean room and more space to play.
check: What happens because of a choice
Can a good choice have a good consequence?
lessons.try: Talk with a grown-up about one rule at home and why it matters.

learn: A citizen is a member of a community, like a town or a country.
Good citizens help others and follow rules.
Even children can be good citizens at home and at school.
lessons.try: Name one thing a good citizen does.

learn: Good citizens are kind. They share, take turns and help.
Good citizens tell the truth, even when it is hard.
Kind words and honest words build trust.
check: What do kind and honest words build?
lessons.try: Do one kind thing for someone today.

learn: Parks, libraries and classrooms are shared places.
Good citizens take care of them. They throw trash away and keep things clean.
When we disagree, we use calm words and listen to each other.
check: How do we take care of shared places?
lessons.try: Pick up three pieces of litter with a grown-up's help.

learn: A community is a place where people live, work and play together.
A community has homes, shops, schools, parks and roads.
People in a community help each other.
check: A place where people live, work and play together
lessons.try: Draw a map of three places in your community.

learn: Firefighters put out fires and help in emergencies.
Police officers help keep people safe and help if you are lost.
Crossing guards help children cross the street.
check: Who can help if you are lost?
Who helps children cross the street?
lessons.try: Act out how a firefighter helps.

lessons.t: Helpers Who Give Us What We Need
learn: Doctors and nurses help us stay healthy. Teachers help us learn.
Farmers grow food. Grocery workers sell it. Mail carriers bring letters and packages.
Every job helps the community in some way.
lessons.try: Ask a grown-up what job they do and how it helps others.

learn: Needs are things we must have to live.
We need food, water, clothing and shelter.
A shelter is a safe place to live, like a house or an apartment.
check: Do we need food to live?
lessons.try: Name the four needs.

learn: Wants are things we would like to have, but we can live without them.
Toys, treats and games are wants.
It is fine to have wants. We just take care of needs first.
lessons.try: Sort pictures into needs and wants.

learn: People work to earn money. They use money to buy needs first, then some wants.
We cannot have everything we want. We have to make choices.
Saving means keeping some money for later, to buy something bigger.
check: Can we have everything we want?
lessons.try: Pretend you have 5 coins. What need and what want would you choose?

learn: A map is a drawing of a place seen from above, like a bird would see it.
A map can show a room, a town, a country or the whole world.
Maps help us find our way.
check: A drawing of a place from above
A room, a town or the whole world
They help us find our way
lessons.try: Draw a map of your bedroom from above.

learn: Maps use small pictures called symbols. A tree symbol can mean a park.
The key tells what each symbol means.
Colours mean things too: blue for water, green for parks.
check: Small pictures that stand for things
lessons.try: Add symbols and a key to your bedroom map.

learn: A globe is a round model of Earth.
Blue shows water. Other colours show land.
Earth has big pieces of land called continents. We live in North America. Earth also has huge oceans.
check: What does blue show on a globe?
lessons.try: Find your continent and an ocean on a globe or map.

learn: The past is what already happened. Yesterday is in the past.
The present is now. Today is the present.
The future is what has not happened yet. Tomorrow is in the future.
lessons.try: Say one thing you did yesterday, one thing you are doing today and one thing you will do tomorrow.

learn: Long ago, life was different. People used candles and oil lamps before electric lights.
Many people travelled by horse or wagon. Clothes were washed by hand.
Children played with simple toys like hoops, marbles and dolls.
check: What did people use before electric lights?
How did many people travel long ago?
Which toy did children play with long ago?
lessons.try: Ask a grandparent or older person what toys they played with.

learn: Some things are still the same today. People still live in families, cook food and play games.
Some things changed. We have cars, computers and electric lights.
Learning about the past helps us understand today.
check: What is still the same today?
lessons.try: Draw a kitchen long ago and a kitchen today.

learn: We live in a country called the United States of America.
A symbol is a picture or thing that stands for an idea.
The American flag has 50 stars and 13 stripes. The stars stand for the 50 states. The stripes stand for the first 13 colonies.
check: How many stars are on the American flag?
What do the 13 stripes stand for?
A picture or thing that stands for an idea
lessons.try: Count the stripes on a picture of the American flag.

lessons.t: The Bald Eagle and the Statue of Liberty
learn: The bald eagle is the national bird. It stands for strength and freedom.
The Statue of Liberty stands in New York Harbor. It welcomes people to the country.
She holds a torch high to light the way.
check: Where is the Statue of Liberty?
What does the Statue of Liberty hold up?
lessons.try: Draw the Statue of Liberty holding her torch.

lessons.t: The Pledge and the Liberty Bell
learn: Many classrooms say the Pledge of Allegiance to show respect for the country.
The Liberty Bell is an old bell in Philadelphia. It has a big crack.
Symbols help people remember important ideas, like freedom and being together.
check: What is special about the Liberty Bell?
lessons.try: Find the Liberty Bell in a picture. Can you see the crack?

learn: A celebration is a happy time to remember something important.
People celebrate with food, music, games and family.
Birthdays are celebrations of the day someone was born.
check: A happy time to remember something important
lessons.try: Tell how you celebrate a birthday.

learn: On July 4 we celebrate Independence Day, the country's birthday, often with parades and fireworks.
Thanksgiving is a day to be thankful and share a meal.
Some days honour people, like Martin Luther King Jr. Day.
check: What do people do on Thanksgiving?
Share a meal and give thanks
lessons.try: Draw a picture of a celebration you have been to.

learn: Families around the world have many holidays.
People may celebrate a new year, a harvest, a festival of lights or a religious holiday.
Learning about other celebrations helps us understand and respect each other.
check: A new year or a harvest
To understand and respect each other
Do all families celebrate the same holidays?
lessons.try: Ask a friend or neighbour about a holiday their family celebrates.
